exchanges: Hey. Got a minute? Three kids, three schedules, and I'm drowning a bit.
Sure, let's untangle it. Who's doing what?
Thandiwe is in grade 9, Sipho is in grade 6, and Nomsa just started grade 1.
Three very different stages. Grade 1 is a big change on its own.
Nomsa loves it. Her teacher Mrs. Pieterse sends home a photo every Friday.
That's a lovely touch. Parents of first graders must appreciate it.
We do. Sipho started soccer again, he's playing goalkeeper this season.
That takes nerve. Is he enjoying it?
So far. His coach is David, a young guy who played at McGill on a scholarship.
Kids tend to love a coach with that kind of background.
They really do. Practices are Tuesday and Thursday at the field behind the library.
Two evenings a week is manageable. Does anyone carpool?
Sometimes Arjun's mom drives. Arjun and Sipho have been friends since kindergarten.
That's a long friendship. A carpool with your best friend is the best kind.
Yes. Thandiwe, on the other hand, is struggling with math this year.
Grade 9 math can be a jump. Is it a particular topic?
Algebra. We hired a tutor, also named David, which the kids think is hilarious.
Two Davids! At least nobody will forget the names.
He's in second year at Waterloo, studying engineering, and he explains things way better than I can.
A student tutor can be great because the material is still fresh for them. Is Thandiwe warming up to him?
Slowly. She's 14, so everything is embarrassing.
Fourteen is peak embarrassment. She'll come around if her grades improve.
She did get a B on her last quiz, so it's working.
That's real progress. Make sure she hears that.
Nomsa wants a tutor now too, just because her sister has one.
Little siblings want everything the older ones have.
She also wants a hamster because her friend Lindiwe got one.
Ah, the friend effect. Are you open to it?
My wife says no. We already have a dog, a big old Labrador called Biscuit.
That's probably enough pet for one house.
Biscuit agrees. Okay, correction from earlier: Sipho isn't in goal. I had it backwards, he's a defender. Arjun is the goalkeeper.
Got it. Did Sipho set you straight?
Loudly. He was offended.
Ha, players take their positions seriously.
Anyway, the school has a science fair next month. Thandiwe wants to do something with bees.
Bees make a great project. Is she thinking about pollination?
Something about why they're dying. My father keeps bees on his farm in Limpopo, so she wants to interview him.
That's a perfect source. A grandfather with hives beats any textbook.
He'll talk her ear off.
That's the best kind of help for a science project.
Sipho wants to build a volcano. Every year.
The volcano is a classic for a reason.
Nomsa just wants to help glue things.
Every project needs a glue helper.
Oh, and my wife just told me her cousin Busisiwe is coming to stay for two weeks. She's a midwife and has night shifts at the hospital here.
That'll be a full house. Night shifts might work out, since she'll be out when the kids are up.
True. She's lovely and the kids adore her.
Then two weeks will fly by.
Let's hope. I need to clear out the spare room tonight.
A good evening project. The kids could help carry things.

questions.message: Where does Thandiwe's tutor go to university?
Nomsa's teacher is Mrs. Pieterse, yeah? I'm writing her a thank-you card.
What does Busisiwe do for work?
I might put a fold-out bed in there for her.
